title: Nonce- and IV-Respecting Authenticated-Encryption Leakage Implications
summary: Encryption-query repetition makes the leakage-security implication trivial without nonce or IV restrictions; prove or refute it under those restrictions and determine whether a general combined leakage function exists.

formal_statement.body: In authenticated-encryption leakage security with nonce-respecting or IV-respecting settings, determine whether $L_E\text{-}\mathrm{IND}\text{-}\mathrm{CPLA} \Longrightarrow (L_E, L_E^0)\text{-}\mathrm{IND}\text{-}\mathrm{aCPLA}$ holds for reasonable leakage sets, given that the encryption-query repetition used in the non-respecting setting is unavailable. Either prove the implication or give a counterexample. More generally, characterize whether for arbitrary leakage sets $L_E$ and $L_D$, there exists a combined leakage function $L_{ED}$ such that $L_{ED}\text{-}\mathrm{IND}\text{-}\mathrm{CPLA}$ implies $(L_E, L_D)\text{-}\mathrm{IND}\text{-}\mathrm{aCPLA}$.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption leakage security and IND-CPLA-to-IND-aCPLA implications under nonce or IV restrictions.
assumptions: The leakage-security setting is nonce-respecting or IV-respecting, making the relevant encryption-query repetition unavailable.
The first implication concerns reasonable leakage sets.
parameters: L_E: a leakage set used in both the CPLA premise and aCPLA target
L_E^0: the second leakage component in the first aCPLA target
L_D: an arbitrary leakage set in the general aCPLA target
L_ED: a sought combined leakage function for the general CPLA premise
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove the restricted-setting implication for reasonable leakage sets or give a counterexample, and determine whether arbitrary L_E and L_D admit an L_ED yielding the general implication.

citations.label: Authenticated Encryption in the Face of Protocol and Side Channel Leakage

progress.summary: The source observes that the implication is trivial when leakage on a valid decryption query can be simulated by repeating the corresponding encryption query, but that this repetition is unavailable in nonce- and IV-respecting settings. It explicitly conjectures the restricted implication for many reasonable leakage sets and asks for a formalization or counterexample, then raises the combined-leakage question more generally.
citation_labels: Guy Barwell et al., Authenticated Encryption in the Face of Protocol and Side Channel Leakage
